title: 新雷
author: 张维屏
intro: Nature has already arranged every flower of spring; all it needs is the first clap of thunder to set them blooming. A cheerful poem about waiting for a new beginning.
analysis: “新雷”是春天的第一声雷。诗人说：大自然不会说话，却很有情意，每当寒冬过去，人们就能感觉到春天来了。后两句很有想象力：千万种红红紫紫的花，大自然早就安排好了，只等新雷响起第一声，它们就一齐开放。这里用了拟人的手法——把“造物”（大自然）写成一个有感情、会安排的人。诗人写的是春雷，心里盼的却不只是春天：他生活在清朝后期，社会沉闷，他盼望像春雷一样的新气象，让人才和新事物像百花一样开放。这首诗明快乐观，“千红万紫”“只待新雷第一声”读起来让人充满希望。
analysisEn: “New thunder” is the first thunder of spring. The poet says that nature never speaks, yet it has feelings: every year, as the cold ends, you can sense spring arriving. The second half is a delightful piece of imagination. Nature has already arranged “a thousand reds and ten thousand purples” — every flower in its place — and is only waiting for the first roll of thunder to let them all bloom. This is personification: 造物, “the Creator” or nature, is treated like a person who cares and makes plans. The poem is about spring thunder, but many readers hear more in it. Zhang Weiping lived in the late Qing, a time that felt stagnant, and he seems to be longing for a fresh start that would let talent and new ideas burst out like spring flowers. Whatever the reading, the tone is bright and hopeful, and the last line — just waiting for the first sound of new thunder — is easy to remember. In the traditional calendar, the first spring thunder is linked with the solar term Jingzhe, “Awakening of Insects”, when everything starts to stir.
background: Zhang Weiping (1780–1859) was a poet and official from Panyu, near Guangzhou. He later lived through the Opium War and wrote poems about it; this short poem welcomes the first thunder of spring.
pronunciation: 却 què。觉 jué（感觉，不读 jiào）。著：安排著，古同“着”，一般注 zhuó（附着、安放），也有读 zhe 的；网站暂注 zhuó。机器朗读已替换。
version: 采用通行文本。“安排著”有的版本写作“安排着”。

lines.py: zào wù wú yán què yǒu qíng
lines.lit: The Creator has no words, yet has feelings;
lines.en: Nature never speaks, yet it cares;

lines.py: měi yú hán jìn jué chūn shēng
lines.lit: each time the cold ends, one feels spring being born.
lines.en: each time the cold is done, you feel spring stir.

lines.py: qiān hóng wàn zǐ ān pái zhuó
lines.lit: A thousand reds, ten thousand purples, all arranged,
lines.en: A thousand reds and purples stand ready in their places,

lines.py: zhǐ dài xīn léi dì yī shēng
lines.lit: only waiting for the first sound of new thunder.
lines.en: waiting only for the first new thunder.

words.note: 古人认为万物由“造物主”创造。现代汉语“造物主”。

words.en: the cold comes to an end

words.note: 今天常说“万紫千红”，是常用成语。

imagery.name: 雷
imagery.zh: 春天第一声雷唤醒万物，也寄托诗人对新气象的期盼。
imagery.en: The first spring thunder wakes all living things — and carries the poet’s hope for a fresh start.

imagery.name: 春
imagery.zh: 寒冬过去、春天来临，是全诗欢快的底色。
imagery.en: The end of winter and the arrival of spring give the poem its happy mood.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 千红万紫的花早已准备好，只等一声令下就开放。
imagery.en: Flowers of every colour stand ready, waiting for the signal to bloom.
